spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the Hawaiian Islands chain from Kauai in the northwest to Hawaii Island in the southeast over dark ocean. Scattered white cumulus and thin cirrus cover parts of the scene with heavier white cloud over and immediately around the islands, especially over the large southeastern island, leaving large areas of open ocean visible in the northeast and center.

plumes.visual_description: narrow diffuse gray-white elongated streak extending south-southwest from the southern tip of the large southeastern island over dark ocean, distinct from brighter puffy cumulus around it

track.note: Centroid drift of a plume still attached to its source is slower than the air; direction is the main signal, speed is approximate.

per_plume.source_hint: downwind lee/wake cloud streaming SW from southern Hawaii Island tip
evidence: USGS HVO valid at image time reports Kilauea not erupting - paused summit eruption in Halema'u'ma'u, ADVISORY/YELLOW - and Mauna Loa not erupting, NORMAL/GREEN, lowering prior for vog from either vent. [E1]

Inferred upwind source end near southern tip of Hawaii Island (18.875N, -155.2E) is 59.7 km from Kilauea summit and 79.3 km from Mauna Loa summit, not anchored at either vent; centroid ~97-98 km from both vents, against a vent-attached vog plume. [E3, E2]

Measured 3-hr drift toward 229 deg SW at ~10.3 km/h with fit R2 0.9 agrees within ~17-25 deg of wind-blown-toward direction (~246 deg from 66 deg at source end, ~254 deg from 74 deg at centroid), supporting passive trade-wind transport of a lee/wake feature off the island tip. [E3, E6, E7]
No FIRMS fire clusters in Hawaii Island box on 2026-08-19; only 99 Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal pixels, providing no detected wildfire source to support wildfire_smoke. [E5]

Mask lies entirely over ocean (land_frac 0.0) extending south-southwest from the island tip as a narrow faint gray-white streak distinct from brighter puffy cumulus in a partly cloudy trade regime, favoring thin lee/wake cloud over vog/smoke. [E4, E3]

Inferred upwind source end near southern tip of Hawaii Island (18.875N, -155.2E) is 59.7 km from Kilauea summit and 79.3 km from Mauna Loa summit, not anchored at either vent; centroid ~97-98 km from both vents, against a vent-attached vog plume.

Measured 3-hr drift toward 229 deg SW at ~10.3 km/h with fit R2 0.9 agrees within ~17-25 deg of wind-blown-toward direction (~246 deg from 66 deg at source end, ~254 deg from 74 deg at centroid), supporting passive trade-wind transport of a lee/wake feature off the island tip.
No FIRMS fire clusters in Hawaii Island box on 2026-08-19; only 99 Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal pixels, providing no detected wildfire source to support wildfire_smoke.

Mask lies entirely over ocean (land_frac 0.0) extending south-southwest from the island tip as a narrow faint gray-white streak distinct from brighter puffy cumulus in a partly cloudy trade regime, favoring thin lee/wake cloud over vog/smoke.

classify.caveats: Single faint streak in GOES-West GeoColor with paused Kilauea eruption; residual degassing cannot be fully excluded and thin vog mixed with cloud is possible, but no eruption and large vent offset argue against vog. No fires detected but small fires below FIRMS detection cannot be ruled out.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Preliminary data indicate the onset of the next fountaining episode is likely between August 21 and August 27. Overview: The summit eruption of Kīlauea in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in July, while the summit region showed patterns of slight inflation. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 57 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the July reporting period, after 94 in June. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
